name: canvas-reveal-effect

frames.best_why: The left card is fully filled with green dots and its title, while the other two stay plain.

tagline: Hovering fills a panel with a burst of tiny glowing dots.
summary: A shader effect that floods its container with a fine grid of dots spreading out from the middle. It appears on hover over a tinted wash and fades away when the pointer leaves.
appearance: Invisible until revealed: then a square fills with a fine grid of tiny glowing dots that gather into a soft cloud near the centre and thin out toward the corners, tinted emerald, pink or blue over a dark wash.
behaviour: Pointing at the card makes the dots pop in from the middle outward in a quick burst, with a title fading in over them. Leaving the card fades the whole field back to an empty panel.
demo_content: Three bordered cards labelled 'Sheetal is Nisha', 'Nisha is Munni' and 'Munni is Aditi', each with a chevron icon.
search_phrases: dots that appear from the center
card that lights up with tiny dots
use_when: A card or panel should reveal a rich particle texture only when the user points at it.
avoid_when: It is a WebGL canvas, so it needs a sized parent and a real GPU for smooth dots.
customise: Set animationSpeed, dotSize, colours and opacities through props, plus a container background class; the intro shader and gradient fade are fixed in the file.
weight_why: A WebGL canvas runs a per-pixel shader at up to 60fps while it is visible.

a11y.note: The reveal is hover-only, so keyboard and touch users never trigger it, and there is no reduced-motion path.

issues: Frame 4 shows the magenta reveal almost invisible against black.
Hover-only reveal leaves touch and keyboard users with a plain empty card.
polish_why: Crisp dot burst and a clear hover reveal; the magenta variant is too dark to read.
title: Canvas Reveal Effect
